# docs_audit_report — 2026-07-02

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — I understand what Carnot does in one sentence
and I can see `pip install carnot-ebm`. But the moment I glance down I hit a
license contradiction (MIT-0 up top, Apache 2.0 in the footer), a "Recent
progress" card wedged sideways into the headline numbers talking about
"Repinned from v2 0.9857", and an Evidence wall of 12 cards full of perfect
1.0 scores and undefined acronyms (FoVer, CCTU, VeriCoT, PREM). A skeptical
engineer keeps the tab open for the hero and then cools off fast — it starts
looking like an internal dashboard that leaked onto the public site.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. LICENSE CONTRADICTION — hero badge + <meta> say "MIT-0"; footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License". A stranger deciding whether they can use this can't
   tell which license applies. (lines 7, 291, 766)
2. RESULTS SECTION READS AS AN INTERNAL BENCHMARK DUMP — 12 cards, several
   with perfect/implausible numbers (1.0, 60/60, a 0.125 "baseline") and a

3. "RECENT PROGRESS" CARD BREAKS THE HERO — a full result card is nested

   ("Repinned from v2 0.9857", "architecture-only 0.8947", "5-seed

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Nav bar (lines 264-277) — 11 text links + 2 buttons — cap at ~5-6. "Get

  Start, Report, Paper, Writing, Roadmap" is an overwhelming menu; a stranger
  reads none of it.
- Results grid (lines 517-577) — 12 cards — a landing page can carry ~5-6
  headline results; 12 near-identical meters means a stranger skims zero.
  Pick the 4-5 strongest and move the rest to the technical report.
- "Recent progress" r-card (line 312) — ~47 words, under the 60 cap, but it
  is misplaced (see Top 3) and jargon-dense, so its real problem isn't length.

### Internal jargon
- Stats label (line 308) + Recent-progress card (line 312) + Preprint (589) —
  "FoVer" — used 4× as the flagship metric anchor, never defined. A stranger

- Recent-progress card (line 312) — "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "architecture-only

- Stats bar (line 306) — "382 Completed milestones" — internal

### Inconsistencies
- LICENSE: "MIT-0" (meta line 7, hero badge line 291) vs "Apache 2.0 License"

### Missing essentials
- License is present but contradictory (see above) — effectively missing a

- Maintainer/affiliation: only "Ian Blenke" in the footer (766). Combined with

- "Why should I trust the numbers?" is asserted (checked-in artifacts, live
  GPU) but undercut by the perfect scores and the unkept provenance-label

### Fabrication signals
- Line 560 — "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — a perfect 1.0 with no
  sample size or caveat.
- Line 565 — "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100% on a 60-item set,
  no false-positive rate shown.
- Line 550 — "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" — a 0.125 AUC baseline is
  *below random chance (0.5)*; presenting a sub-chance baseline to make the
  delta look huge is exactly what a hostile reviewer pounces on.
- Line 570 — "0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings" — headlining a
  literal zero-accuracy-change result reads as padding the evidence count.
- Line 431 — "99.3% of wrong code flagged" — plausible, but sits next to the
  above, so it inherits the skepticism.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero nails the one-sentence "what is this": the 47+28=76 example and
  "second pair of eyes" framing are clear to a non-specialist, and

- The "How it works: Extract → Check → Repair" bento and the Python quickstart

- The blog section is a real strength: honest, self-critical titles ("Caught
  Cheating", "Two Retractions and a Rescue", "Why We Report Two AUROCs Now")
  signal integrity and make the project feel alive and trustworthy.
